tasks.short: Develop a program plan for a resident in the house.

steps.what: Read the house activity aims in the {DOCS}
Develop the program with the resident in the house
Draft an unsaved program plan from those aims, then stop

loop.input: the resident program aims and the house activity aims
loop.output: an unsaved program plan whose activities each name one aim
loop.check: drop any activity that names no aim from the meeting note
loop.why_not_simpler: The meeting note is free text. A field copy cannot write the activities.

steps.what: Check each program activity against that resident aim, then accept
Store only the accepted program plan in the {DOCS}

tasks.design: She develops the program with the resident in the house, and that meeting stays hers. A bounded loop drafts an unsaved program plan from the house activity aims in the {DOCS} and her meeting note, then stops. She checks that each activity is what that aim means for this resident, and only the accepted plan is stored in the house program file in the {DOCS}, which is the copy other staff follow.
tasks.previous_blocker: The aims come from a meeting in her own words, and a plan other staff follow cannot be stored before she has checked the fit.
tasks.enabler_now: A short loop can name activities from a meeting note and an aim list, then stop, while the document store already keeps the house program file.
tasks.still_hard: Judging whether an activity fits this resident, and the meeting itself, stay with her.
tasks.human_edge: She knows whether an activity fits this resident this week, including when the note is thin.
tasks.altitude: The meeting stays hers. She no longer composes the program plan from scratch. She still accepts or rejects every activity before other staff follow the stored plan.

reach.task: Develop a program of activities for a child in their care.
reach.learn: Which house aim must be named before an activity is stored for others to follow.

evidence.claim: A bounded loop can draft activities that each name an aim already written in the meeting note. It cannot judge whether the activity fits the resident.
EU AI Act Annex III point 3 covers assignment to education and evaluating learning outcomes.
An application that time-stamps each staff action can monitor performance and needs works-council consent under WOR art. 27.

assumptions: House activity aims are named entries in the {DOCS}: aim name and house group. The meeting step produces a short note, the resident program aims, which she already writes while developing the program. That note's time stays in the meeting at full remaining time.
If the note names no aim, the draft is empty and she writes the plan during the check. The 4 rewrite hours are that case in a thin week, already taken off the central 22.
Storing the plan is work she does today so other house staff can follow it. It is not a second save of a plan she already wrote in full, and she does not approve a private note.
The plan does not score the resident and does not assign a school place. Health detail stays out of this draft. A message to a parent or another school is not built.
The store does not time-stamp her actions as a performance score.
unknowns: Whether this house keeps activity aims as named entries or only as prose.
Whether other staff are required to follow the stored program plan.
research_questions: Are house activity aims stored as named entries before a program meeting?
Who, other than the advisor, reads the stored program plan?

already_counted.description: She checks each activity against the resident's aim and accepts or rejects the plan.

incremental.description: She rewrites activities the check rejects when the meeting note was too thin.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: In a week where the meeting note names no usable aim, the draft is empty and she writes the plan while checking, so about 8 remains after the 4 rewrite hours already taken off the central 22. In a week where the note names specific aims, about 14 remains. The 12 check hours stay in the check step.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Give requested progress information on the case plan.

steps.what: Read the students' progress entries in the {DOCS}
Read the requested progress note in the {DOCS}
Draft an unsaved progress account from the entries, then stop

loop.input: the progress entries and the progress request
loop.output: an unsaved progress account, each sentence citing one entry
loop.check: drop any sentence that cites no progress entry
loop.why_not_simpler: The entries are free text. Copying the request cannot state the progress.

steps.what: Check each sentence is what the progress entry says, then accept
Store only the accepted progress account in the {DOCS}
Tell the requester the students' progress account in the house

tasks.design: She reads the students' progress entries and the request in the {DOCS}. A bounded loop drafts an unsaved progress account from those entries and stops. She checks that each sentence is what the entry says and that it answers the request, stores only the accepted account on the case plan in the {DOCS}, and tells the requester in the house.
tasks.previous_blocker: Progress entries are prose, and a sentence that overstates a student can harm them if it is stored or said.
tasks.enabler_now: A short loop can tie each sentence to an entry that is already on the case plan, then stop, and the case plan already lives in the document store.
tasks.still_hard: Judging whether the sentence is fair, and telling the requester, stay with her.
tasks.human_edge: She knows whether a sentence is fair to the student and whether it answers what was asked.
tasks.altitude: The talk with the requester stays hers. She no longer composes the progress account from scratch. She still accepts every sentence before it is stored on the case plan.

reach.task: Report how a resident took part in a recreation session.
reach.learn: Cite the progress entry the sentence comes from before the account is stored on the case plan.

evidence.claim: A bounded loop can draft progress sentences that cite an existing entry. It cannot judge whether the sentence answers the request.
EU AI Act Annex III point 3 covers assignment to education and evaluating learning outcomes.
An application that time-stamps each staff action can monitor performance and needs works-council consent under WOR art. 27.

assumptions: Progress entries, each a date and a short fact or a prose line, are already in the case plan in the {DOCS} before this task. This task does not create those entries. The request is a short written ask already stored with the case plan.
If the entries are missing or undated prose she cannot cite, the draft is empty and she writes the account during the check. The 5 rewrite hours are already taken off the central 26.
Storing the account on the case plan is work she does today so colleagues can read how the plan developed. It is not a second save of an account she already wrote in full.
The account does not score learning. A letter or email to a parent, a school, or an outside clinician is not built and would be its own gated send. Telling the requester in the house is not a send.
The store does not time-stamp her actions as a performance score.
unknowns: Whether progress entries already exist before a request, or she gathers them only when asked.
Whether the requester is a colleague in the house or a parent who expects a written copy.
research_questions: Are progress entries dated facts on the case plan before a request arrives?
Is the usual requester present in the house, or do they expect a message sent out?

already_counted.description: She checks each sentence against the progress entry and the request, then accepts the account.

incremental.description: She rewrites sentences the check rejects when the entries do not support them.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When progress entries are missing or undated prose, the draft is empty and about 8 remains after the 5 rewrite hours already taken off the central 26. When each entry has a date and a fact she can cite, about 16 remains. The 14 check hours stay in the check step.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Confer with medical personnel about a resident's needs.

steps.what: Read the residents' needs in the care record ({OTHER})
Confer with medical personnel on the residents' backgrounds and needs
Write the residents' understood needs into the care record ({OTHER})

tasks.design: She reads the resident care record ({OTHER}) and confers with medical personnel in person. She writes what she understood back into that care record herself. There is no draft and no separate store, because writing the note and keeping it are the same act, and nothing was recorded that a model could read.
tasks.previous_blocker: What medical personnel say is spoken in the room. Without a recording there is no text to draft from, and a recording of this conference is not assumed.
tasks.enabler_now: Nothing new makes the conference itself faster. The care record already holds the note she writes.
tasks.still_hard: Hearing what the clinician means for this resident, and writing it accurately, stay with her.
tasks.human_edge: She hears what the clinician means for this resident and what she should do differently tonight.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes. The conference and the need note stay hers, and she gains no decision right.

reach.task: Pass a child's health needs to the next adult in the house.
reach.learn: Keep the health note in the care record. Do not send it out as a message.

evidence.claim: Without a recording, a model cannot draft what medical personnel said in the room.
Health notes are special-category data, and pasting them into a general chatbot means a processor without a contract.
An application that time-stamps each staff action can monitor performance and needs works-council consent under WOR art. 27.

assumptions: The conference is in person at the residence or the clinic. Medical personnel may be outside the organisation. The talk is not a send, and no message to a clinic is built.
No recording is made. She writes the need note herself into the resident care record ({OTHER}). Writing it and keeping it are one act, so there is no gated store and no self-approval of a save.
No software is built, so upkeep is zero. The note is not pasted into a chatbot. The design does not log the conference as a performance score of the advisor.
unknowns: Whether medical personnel are employed by the residence or by an outside practice.
Whether the house requires a written note after every conference.
research_questions: Is a written note of the conference required, and where does it live?
Are the medical personnel staff of this organisation?

incremental.description: No machine runs on the conference, so upkeep is zero.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The conference and the need note stay hers. Nothing is drafted or stored by a machine, so the saving is 0 for both a short call and a long meeting. No upkeep hours are added.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Decide and record a disciplinary or corrective action.

steps.what: Read the house rules and the incident in the {DOCS}
Hear the resident before any disciplinary or corrective action
Decide the disciplinary or corrective action herself
Draft an unsaved corrective record from her decision, then stop
Check the record matches the corrective action she decided, then accept
Store only the accepted corrective action in the {DOCS}
Tell the resident the disciplinary actions in the house

tasks.design: She hears the resident and decides the disciplinary or corrective action herself. A field copy drafts an unsaved record from the action type, the rule, the date, and her one-line reason, then stops. She checks that the record matches the action she decided, and only that accepted record is stored in the conduct file in the {DOCS}. She tells the resident in the house.
tasks.previous_blocker: The action depends on what she heard, and a conduct record that names the wrong rule is hard to undo.
tasks.enabler_now: Once she has named the action type and the rule, copying those fields into the conduct file is configuration of the document store. Choosing the action is not.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing the action, hearing the resident, and telling them stay with her.
tasks.human_edge: She chooses an action that fits what she heard and the house rules, including when to recommend rather than impose one.
tasks.altitude: Hearing the resident, choosing the action, and telling them stay hers. She no longer copies the action into the conduct file by hand. She still accepts the record before it is stored, and the copy does not choose the action.

reach.role: First-Line Supervisors of Personal Service Workers
reach.task: Review a corrective action after the advisor has chosen it.
reach.learn: Read the stored conduct record, which copies the advisor's decision and does not choose the action.

evidence.claim: Copying an action type, a rule id, a date, and a one-line reason into a conduct record is deterministic. Choosing the disciplinary action is not.
An application that time-stamps each staff action can monitor performance and needs works-council consent under WOR art. 27.

assumptions: When she decides, she sets action type, rule id, resident, date, and a one-line reason. That capture sits in the decision step at full remaining time. The draft only copies those fields and does not choose the action.
If she decides in the room and sets no fields, the copy is empty and she writes the record during the check. The 3 rewrite hours are already taken off the central 14.
Storing the conduct record is work she does today so the house can see the action later. It is not a second save of a note she already wrote in full, and there is no approval of a private note.
A report to the police, a parent, or a school is not built and would be its own gated send. Telling the resident in the house is not a send.
The conduct record is about the resident's action, not a performance score of the advisor, and it does not time-stamp her work.
unknowns: Whether a supervisor must confirm the action before the conduct record is stored. That confirmation is not in this task.
Which fields she actually sets at the moment she decides.
research_questions: Does she name an action type and a rule id when she decides, or only speak the decision?
Must someone else confirm a corrective action before it is stored?

already_counted.description: She checks the draft record against the action she decided, then accepts it.

incremental.description: She rewrites the record when the copied rule or action type does not match her decision.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When she decides in the room and writes no action type or rule, the copy is empty and about 3 remains after the 3 rewrite hours already taken off the central 14. When those fields are set, about 8 remains. The 12 check hours stay in the check step.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Her week keeps the program meeting, the progress conversation, the medical conference, and the choice of corrective action. Saved time is only the composition and storage of the program plan, the progress account, and the conduct record. She still accepts those three before they are stored.
reach: First-Line Supervisors of Personal Service Workers
skills_to_grow: Reject a program activity that is not the aim the resident just stated.
Reject a progress sentence the entry does not say, and a conduct record that names a rule she did not choose.
role.ambitious_version: The house program plan, the progress account, and the conduct record are drafted for her to accept. The program meeting, the progress conversation, the medical conference, and the disciplinary decision stay hers.
